name: bucket_count_upper
doc:
The rounded bucket count satisfies `B κ ≤ m κ * κ + 1`; glue for the JLS allocation.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Read the rounded quotient, apply the public natural-division bound, and use W≥1.

name: bucket_count_lower
doc:
The rounded bucket count covers the allocation: `m κ * κ ≤ B κ * W κ`; glue.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Apply the public strict quotient bound, clear its additive rounding term, then use the max bound.

name: prefactor_eventually_le_two_pow
doc:
The construction prefactor `(κ+1)*B κ+1` is eventually at most `2^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Bound the prefactor by the stored output polynomial. Apply PolyExpr.eval_le and the existing polynomial-over-exponential limit, then choose a common cutoff.
probe_supersession: Unused namespace open removed; statement/imports unchanged; invalid exact retained and invalid apply not run.

name: binomial_ratio_quarter
doc:
For positive B,r with `4*exp(1)*N ≤ B*r` and `κ ≤ r`, the ratio `choose(N,r)/B^r` is at most `4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Use binomial_bound once, divide the resulting power by B^r, bound its base by 1/4, then lower the exponent using the public ordered-power lemma.

name: smallset_bucket_tail_quarter
doc:
For κ≥12 and Γ κ≤B κ, every fixed set of size at most Γ κ has some overloaded bucket with probability at most `B κ * 4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Use the exact finite bucket-tail bound. The cardinality and bucket hypotheses give the base inequality for binomial_ratio_quarter at r=κ+1.

name: capacity_bucket_tail_quarter
doc:
For κ≥12, uniform placement exceeds the rounded capacity in some bucket with probability at most `B κ * 4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Use the full-load bound, bucket_count_lower and the capacity reader to verify the base inequality, then apply binomial_ratio_quarter.

name: cond1_single_le_quarter
doc:
If `4*cLoc ≤ log₂(n κ)`, one fixed-index bad-count failure has probability at most 1/4.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Combine the existing Markov bound with the public quotient rounding bound for Γ. Cast the resulting natural inequality and clear the positive denominator.

name: cond1_repetitions_fixed_index
doc:
At a fixed complete index, the probability that every independent repetition satisfies Cond1 is at most `4⁻¹^κ`, under the logarithmic locality bound.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Discard each unused secret by the product probability reader. Reuse OneWay.uprob_pi_forall for the independent repetitions, then apply the single-repetition bound.

name: cond1_all_fixed_index
doc:
Under the logarithmic locality bound, the full seed-core law at each fixed index has simultaneous Cond1 probability at most `4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Read the full seed sampler as its exact uniform draw, transport through sdCore_draw, discard the Boolean seed, and apply the fixed-index repetition bound.

name: cond1_all_joint
doc:
Under the logarithmic locality bound, simultaneous Cond1 under the actual joint law has probability at most `4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Condition on the complete index, apply the same fixed-index bound to every section, and average over the actual index sampler using expectation monotonicity.

name: cond3_joint_le_quarter_pow
doc:
For κ≥12, common capacity failure under the actual joint law has probability at most `B κ * 4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Discard the unused full seed draw and the unused generator/matrix coordinates through the probability readers, then apply the uniform full-load bound.

name: cond2_sparse_joint_le_quarter_pow
doc:
For κ≥12 and Γ κ≤B κ, each joint Cond2-and-not-Cond1 event has probability at most `B κ * 4⁻¹^κ`.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 20-21]. This is theorem-only analytic glue;
no sampling or efficiency construction is introduced.

**Proof sketch.** Transport the actual index/core draws through explicit product equivalences so placement is last. Fix all other data, use the fixed small-set bound when its cardinality is at most Γ, handle the impossible case by zero, and average the section bounds.

name: jointLaw_prob_eq_uprob
marker: /-- Error probability is the exact chance
doc:
The probability of any event under jointLaw equals its probability after the index and seed cores are applied to one uniform raw product draw.
[JLS26, proof of Claim 4.2, pp. 19-21]; semantic probability reader glue.

**Proof sketch.** Read the two deterministic pushforwards through the public expectation rules. Combine the independent raw draws with Bridge.prob_sample_pair and finish with the uniform probability reader.

doc:
The scalar noise law also holds when the explicit product seed is cast into the stored coin type.
[JLS26, before Definition 2.3, p. 9]; cast-indexed reader glue.

**Proof sketch.** Reuse lpnNoise_law and Core.cast_eq in the noise owner. The published statement exposes the cast normalization needed by foreign consumers without unfolding the noise definition.
